reviews.text:
Be careful before subscribing. The app showed me a page saying I would get a 7-day free trial, so I went ahead and subscribed. Instead, I was immediately charged $40 for the full year. No trial at all.

I had used a trial before, so maybe I wasn't eligible for another one. That's fine, but then why show me a page saying I'm getting a 7-day trial? If I'm not eligible, the app should clearly say that before I subscribe instead of advertising a trial that I won't actually get.

I don't know if this is a bug or intentional, but either way it's incredibly misleading. Looking at other reviews, I actually found some people mentioned the same problem nearly a year ago, and it still hasn't been fixed. I only made the purchase because the app told me there was a trial.

reviews.title: Pretty good, one big pitfall
reviews.text:
I appreciate that this app is streamlined, and easy to use. It would be great if it tracked fat as a macro.

One thing to watch out for is the  “Recent Meals” feature on food tracking. Understand that it is not just a list of foods in standard serving sizes, but macros for the food in the quantity you last recorded. 

For example, you search the database and find the information for one cup of whole milk. But you drink a half a cup of milk and so record .5 servings. Now the .5 servings is the nutritional information stored in “Recent Meals.” 

The next time you pull whole milk off “Recent Meals” for a new diary entry it will pull that half cup “meal” up and show it as one serving. If you assume, as I did, that was indicating the standard serving from the nutritional database (1 cup) you will be off by 50%.

What would be more useful, in my opinion, is
Quick access to “Recent FOODS,” with the macros corresponding to a standard serving size that is easy to see: “Whole Milk, 1c.” 

The way it is now you have to look up everything every time, which is a drag.

reviews.title: Has potential, but “unique” features don’t work right.
reviews.text:
I do like the app and had high hopes, but… 

The name “pep” is the medical abbreviation for post-exposure prophylaxis, which is a treatment for someone who may have been exposed to HIV. The name has nothing to do with GLP-1. The name has caused some confusion in my GLP-1 community, as well as with my medical provider.

One of the big differences from pep and one of its main competitors is that you can log meals/macros on pep in more detail. But the interface is wonky and the maths aren’t mathing. It took me over half an hour to enter a day’s worth of meals, and that was only because I gave up, deleted everything, and entered everything manually. Example: tried to use entry for tilapia filets, 1 is 90 calories, 20g protein. I had 2 filets so adjusted the quantity to 2, so it should read 180 / 40, but it said 360 / 80. If the app can’t do simple math multiplying calories x 2, then how can I trust it with my medical information like shot dosages, weight calculation, percentages, etc.?

Also, if you enter your meal entries out of chronological order, it saves them in the order you entered them - it doesn’t arrange them by time.

For $40 a year, not worth it. I can pay less to get features that don’t require all the manual work or just use a food logging app with an easier interface.

reviews.text: I’m so happy I came across this app! I personally love the reminders for shot day and water intake. I have been using the app for about one month and love the accountability it provides on this journey. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Great GLP1 Tracking App
reviews.text: This is a well thought out out app! It has great features. Seems to work seamlessly as well. For anyone who is a tracker and needs the data, this is for you! Affordable and worth it!

reviews.title: Best GLP1 tracking app!
reviews.text: Pep has been a game changer on my glp1 journey by helping me stay organized and keeping me on top of all my health goals. The fact that there’s a one stop shop for logging everything I need INCLUDING my injections makes my life SO much easier. Thank you, Pep!

reviews.title: New customer
reviews.text: Loving the app so far, especially when I go to my endocrinologist and they ask me different questions. Everything is right and my fingertips, but the only thing is that the notetaking is not in the same spot of where I put my weight. Log kind of hard to figure out where to go back to read a previous note

reviews.title: My Go-To Tracking App
reviews.text: I love that everything is in a single app. No more juggling several different apps to keep track of my injections, weight, protein, and progress photos! It’s important to me to document the weight loss process on a GLP-1 and Pep makes it so easy.

reviews.title: Great App
reviews.text: This app is by far the best I’ve ever come across when it comes to my Glp-1 journey

reviews.title: Love this app!!
reviews.text: Keeps thing easy and simple for logging all of my shots and weight changes!! I’ll never lose track of my shot day and i love that i can easily log my water and protein intake!

reviews.title: Buggy
reviews.text: The app itself is great but I have to recreate my profile every time I use it….i wish it would keep my profile logged in to store data. A bit frustrating.

reviews.title: Easy to use tracking app
reviews.text: Love how easy it is to log my shots and view how much medication is in my system. This has made my glp-1 way easier.
